what: The media-kit track's candidate batch, rounds one and two. STAGED, NOT WIRED: nothing under public/design/ is read by any marketing surface and marketing-media.test.ts does not scan it. These files exist so the board at /design/c/media-kit can show a candidate beside the frame it would replace, with its provenance under it.
schema: Every record carries the six fields the proposed rule adds to a MARKETING_IMAGES entry: author, sourceUrl, license, clause, retrieved and people. clause is the sentence of the license that permits the use, quoted; people is none, unidentifiable or identifiable and is the field that decides whether a frame may sit on a page that makes a claim (rule 1.4). provenance.test.ts pins every field here against candidates.ts and refuses a record with a field missing.
license: Every file is CC0 1.0. The Commons file page carries the Unsplash template, which Commons applies only to media published on Unsplash before 5 June 2017, when its sitewide license was CC0; the API reports CC0 for the file.
caveat: CC0 waives copyright. It does not waive publicity or privacy rights, and Commons verifies no uploader's ownership. A frame whose people field reads identifiable needs a release nobody here holds. See docs/specs/media-kit.md 1.4.
resized: Each file is the Commons thumbnail of the original, resized to 1200 px on the long edge and re-encoded for the web with all metadata stripped. CC0 permits modification without permission; the record of who made it lives here rather than in EXIF.
